    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x ∂γ O)) (Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))) ∧
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x * p O x)) (Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))) ∧

      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x ∂γ O) ∂(Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))) = v ∧

decoder_context: EuclideanSpace real (Fin n) is real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard l2 norm. Fin n indexes coordinates from zero through n-1. WithLp.ofLp y j is coordinate j of y.

Real powers use Real.rpow, defined for all real bases. Real division and inverse are totalized at zero. All n/2 dimension exponents use real division; natural powers have natural exponents. Integrable means genuine real Bochner absolute integrability under the displayed measure. No L1 fact or moment value is a supplied premise.
The orthogonal group is full real O(n), both determinant signs, with its matrix Borel structure. Measure.haarMeasure(top : PositiveCompacts G) is canonical normalized full-group Haar probability.

The existing multivariateGaussian zero covariance C is the pushforward of canonical stdGaussian by z -> Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (CFC.sqrt C) z. Matrix inverse denotes the nonsingular matrix inverse. All displayed integral measures and density factors retain their literal meaning; no new Gaussian law is defined.

/-! The evaluated signed Gaussian expectation in Appendix B.2.2, Eq24.
The normalized spherical numerator, the actual Gaussian-to-surface transport,
and the actual density law are canonical dependencies. -/

theorem selected_gaussian_value {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) :
    let s : ℝ := Real.sqrt κ
    let r : ℝ := (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) * ((s - 1) / (s + 1))
    let ℓ : ℝ := (4 * (n : ℝ) * s + (s - 1) ^ 2) /
      (8 * (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) - 1))
    let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
    let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
      fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
        Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
          (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
    let t : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2)
    let v : ℝ := ((-1 : ℝ) ^ n / (n : ℝ)) * ((s - 1) / (s + 1)) ^ n *
      (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) / (1 - r ^ 2)
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x ∂γ O)) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x * p O x)) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x ∂γ O) ∂orthogonalHaar n) = v ∧
    (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x * p O x) ∂orthogonalHaar n) = v := by
  let s : ℝ := Real.sqrt κ
  let r : ℝ := (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) * ((s - 1) / (s + 1))
  let ℓ : ℝ := (4 * (n : ℝ) * s + (s - 1) ^ 2) /
    (8 * (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) - 1))
  let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
    fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
      (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
  let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
    fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
      Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
        (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
  let t : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2)
  let v : ℝ := ((-1 : ℝ) ^ n / (n : ℝ)) * ((s - 1) / (s + 1)) ^ n *
    (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) / (1 - r ^ 2)
  change Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
      (∫ x, t x ∂γ O)) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
      (∫ x, t x * p O x)) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x ∂γ O)
      ∂orthogonalHaar n) = v ∧
    (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x * p O x)
      ∂orthogonalHaar n) = v
  have ht := SelectedTilt.selected_tilt hn hκ
  have hg := GaussianExpectation.actual_gaussian_transform hn hκ
    (ℓ := ℓ) ht.2.2.1.le
  have hpoint : (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x ∂γ O)) =ᵐ[
      orthogonalHaar n]
      (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x * p O x)) :=
    Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun O => congrArg
      (fun z => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * z) (hg.1 O).2.2
  have hvalue : (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * (∫ x, t x ∂γ O)
      ∂orthogonalHaar n) = v := by
    have hs := (SurfaceLaw.selected_surface_transport hn hκ).2.2.2
    have hm := (selected_numerator_value hn hκ).2
    rw [hm] at hs
    calc
      _ = (((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (s - 1) ^ (n - 1)) / (s + 1) ^ n) *
          (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
          (-(s - 1) / ((n : ℝ) * (1 - r ^ 2))) := hs
      _ = v := by
        have hn0 : (n : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : n ≠ 0)
        have hsp : s + 1 ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (by dsimp [s]; positivity)
        have hden : 1 - r ^ 2 ≠ 0 := by
          have hr : 0 < r := ht.1
          have hr1 : r < 1 := ht.2.1
          nlinarith
        have hpow (a : ℝ) : a ^ n = a ^ (n - 1) * a := by
          conv_lhs => rw [← Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega : 1 ≤ n)]
          rw [pow_succ]
        dsimp only [v]
        rw [div_pow, hpow (-1), hpow (s - 1)]
        field_simp
  exact ⟨hg.2.1, hg.2.1.congr hpoint, hvalue,
    (integral_congr_ae hpoint.symm).trans hvalue⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.EvaluatedGaussian

reconstruction.text:
For every natural number n with 3 ≤ n and every real number κ with 4 ≤ κ, let E be real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard ℓ2 norm and coordinates indexed by Fin n = {0, …, n−1}. Let G be the full real orthogonal group O(n), with both determinant signs and its matrix Borel structure, and let μ be Measure.haarMeasure(⊤ : PositiveCompacts G), the canonical normalized Haar probability measure on that full group. Set
s = √κ,
r = (1 − 1/n)((s − 1)/(s + 1)),
ℓ = (4ns + (s − 1)²)/(8n(n − 1)),
with n interpreted as a real number in these expressions.

For each O ∈ G, identify O with its real n by n matrix and define
A_O = ((κ + 1)/2) I − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ).
Let γ_O be the existing multivariateGaussian measure with mean 0 ∈ E and covariance argument A_O⁻¹. This means exactly the pushforward of canonical stdGaussian by z ↦ Matrix.toEuclideanCLM(CFC.sqrt(A_O⁻¹)) z; matrix inverse is the nonsingular matrix inverse in the approved definition context. Define the real function p_O on E by
p_O(x) = √(det A_O)/(2π)^(n/2) · exp(−(x · (A_O x))/2),
where x · (A_O x) is the coordinate dot product of WithLp.ofLp x with A_O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x. Also define
t(x) = exp(−ℓ ‖x‖²)
and the real number
v = ((−1)^n/n) ((s − 1)/(s + 1))^n (1 − 1/n)^(n/2)/(1 − r²).

Both real-valued functions on G,
O ↦ det(O) · (∫_E t(x) dγ_O(x))
and
O ↦ det(O) · (∫_E t(x)p_O(x) dx),
are absolutely Bochner integrable with respect to μ. Here dx in the second inner integral is the standard Euclidean Lebesgue volume measure on E, and every displayed integral is a real Bochner integral. Moreover, the following two equalities each hold:
∫_G det(O) · (∫_E t(x) dγ_O(x)) dμ(O) = v,
∫_G det(O) · (∫_E t(x)p_O(x) dx) dμ(O) = v.

The exponents n in (−1)^n and ((s − 1)/(s + 1))^n are natural powers. Each exponent n/2 is real division and uses Real.rpow, defined for all real bases; each square has natural exponent 2. Real division and inverse retain their totalized Lean meaning. The two integrability conclusions concern the displayed functions of O; the statement does not separately assert integrability of any inner integrand. The function p_O and the measure γ_O retain their literal displayed definitions, with no additional density identification needed as a premise or added as a conclusion.
